_comment: CLICKTON - the little city made entirely of small colourful bricks. The ground is a studded baseplate, the roads and pavements are flat plates, the buildings are brick courses under studded roofs, the trees and props are built piece by piece, and every visitor (you, your companion, everyone else) is rebuilt out of bricks by the world's actor_look. No people and no creatures: just the city, tidy and lit and waiting. Its SECRET: one single rainbow brick set into the front wall of the Crooked Cottage at the quiet west end of the Quay Lane. Generated by tools/gen_clickton_world.py (art: pokepals/tools/gen_clickton.py over tools/brickart) - edit that and re-run, don't hand-tune positions.
intro: Everything here is made of bricks, and so, you notice, are you. Touch things. Look low down. One of the bricks is not like the others.

props.label: a mailbox
props.lore: A mailbox. Inside, one letter, addressed to "Whoever Lives Here". It says: "Welcome. It's lovely. Don't mind the corners."

props.label: a fire hydrant
props.lore: It has never once been used. It is very proud of this, and stands a little straighter than the other hydrants.

props.label: a traffic cone
props.lore: Somebody put a cone here, years ago, for a reason that has since built itself into the road.

props.label: a signpost of studs
props.lore: WELCOME TO CLICKTON, says the sign, in raised white studs. Underneath, in smaller ones: "Population: you. Please touch the bricks. They like it."

props.label: a bench on the quay
props.lore: A bench built for two, or one person and a very large dog. The bay laps against the baseplate just beyond it, studs and all.

props.label: a bench on the quay
props.lore: Somebody has left one single brick on the seat, as if saving it. It's yellow. You put it back exactly where it was.

props.label: a very large brick duck
props.lore: A duck of yellow bricks on a grey plinth, mid-quack. It is the only duck in Clickton, which is why it's allowed to be this big.

props.label: a little boat
props.lore: A boat made of eleven bricks and a very good mast. It bobs a stud's width up and down, which is the most a brick can manage.

props.label: a boat tied to the pier
props.lore: It's tied to the pier with a brick on a string. The boat has never gone anywhere. It's the thought of leaving that matters.

props.label: a stack of crates on the pier
props.lore: Crates of loose bricks, labelled with colours: RED (MOSTLY). BLUE (SOME). YELLOW (ONE, PROBABLY A MISTAKE).

props.label: a barrel
props.lore: It rattles. Whatever's inside has a great many corners.

props.label: a small sign by the lighthouse
props.lore: THE LIGHTHOUSE. Its lamp is one clear yellow brick, and every night it shines exactly as far as the end of the pier, which is exactly as far as it needs to.

props.label: the fountain
props.lore: A fountain of grey bricks around a blue plate, with a spout of pale plates that never moves and never runs dry. Wishes go in the bowl. They're all the same wish: more bricks.

props.label: a plaque in the square
props.lore: THE FIRST BRICK. "When Clickton was begun there was one brick, and it was every colour at once. The builder was so fond of it that, rather than waste it on a corner, they set it into a wall, low down where a hand could find it, and told nobody which wall. It never stopped swirling. They say it's near a quiet end of town, by the water."

props.label: a smaller brick duck
props.lore: The big duck on the quay has a cousin. This one is pink, and the size of a cat, and it is very, very pleased to be here.

props.label: a small sign by the clock tower
props.lore: THE CLOCK TOWER. The clock is always exactly right, because it's the only one in Clickton, and so it's the one deciding.

props.label: a slide
props.lore: A slide of blue plates, stepping down. Going down it makes a sound in your head, a soft ker-lik-lik-lik-lik, one for every stud.

props.label: a seesaw
props.lore: It's balanced exactly level. It has been exactly level for as long as anyone can remember, which is a form of quiet joy.

props.label: a picnic table
props.lore: A table with a red-and-white cloth made of red and white plates. Somebody has laid out a picnic of tiny bricks. It looks delicious, if you are a brick.

props.label: a planter
props.lore: The flowers in this one are in rainbow order. Somebody took care.

props.label: a sign at the lane's end
props.lore: QUAY LANE. The shops here sell bricks by the colour, by the stud, and, on request, by the feeling. A little card says: "ASK FOR THE ONE THAT'S BEEN WAITING."

props.label: a sign at a corner
props.lore: HIGH LANE. The buildings get taller toward the north, and the lane gets no wider, which is how it ended up so pleasantly shady.

props.label: the Brickworks sign
props.lore: THE BRICKWORKS. Every brick in Clickton was made here, once, in the same kiln. They all came out a different colour. Nobody has ever worked out why, and everyone is rather glad.

props.label: a sign under the tall buildings
props.lore: THE SKYLINE. Thirty-two floors of someone's idea of 'high up'. The lifts are very polite, and in no hurry.

props.label: a planter
props.lore: A box of bricks with flowers made of smaller bricks, which need no water and are never any trouble.

_secret_comment: This world's one SECRET (docs/home-world-and-secrets-design.md): 'reveal' is 'always' (it is simply there to be found). The brick is painted by the cottage's BuildingView 'inlay' (not by WorldArt, which would draw it under the building); the world's art lists 'rainbow_brick' as an 'unseen' prop type for exactly that reason.

secret.lore: One brick, set into the wall among all the others, low down where a hand would find it. It fits as if it had always been part of the building, but every colour there is turns slowly through it, round and round, and it's very slightly warm.
secret.found_line: The first brick of Clickton, every colour at once. It comes out of the wall with a small, happy click.

keepsake.label: the first brick
keepsake.line: Your companion sniffs the little rainbow brick, then sits down very close to it, the way you sit by something that matters.

portals.label: the way back to the Vale
